title: Exam day
lede: What the app does to the iPad, and what happens when a student gets locked out.

blocks.text: Students sit the exam in **Examplify**, the ExamSoft app for iPad. You will not usually be in the room, but the questions students ask you afterwards will be about what happens in it.
Once the exam starts, Examplify takes over the device. Screenshots, copy and paste, and internet access all stop working until the exam ends. Nothing else on the iPad is reachable.

blocks.title: Button combinations can lock a student out
blocks.text: Press enough button combinations on the iPad and Examplify locks the student out of the exam. Getting back in needs a universal code, also called an exam resume code. The proctor holds it, printed on the PowerPoint OME prepares for that sitting.

blocks.title: Codes are not in this repository
blocks.text: Exam passwords and universal resume codes belong to a specific sitting and live on the OME proctor materials for it. They are never committed here.

items: Shut it down and restart it at least once, which clears most technical problems before they happen.
Download the exam when the window opens rather than on the morning of the exam.

blocks.text: OME prints two hard copies of every exam, which cover device failure and in-house exam takers. A student whose iPad fails mid-exam should tell the proctor straight away rather than troubleshoot, because the paper copy and the resume code are both in the room.

blocks.title: Nobody can open the exam early
blocks.text: A student can hold the downloaded file for 48 hours and still not open it. The exam stays sealed until the proctor announces the password.
